executive_summary: Two-to-four sentences for a non-technical reader: what was assessed, the most important risks, and what to do first.
posture_statement: Analyst judgement of overall posture with reasons. Never state that the application is secure.

findings.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can read any invoice
findings.description: GET /api/invoices/:id loads the invoice by primary key without checking that invoice.accountId matches the caller's account.
findings.evidence: src/routes/invoices.js:42 `Invoice.findByPk(req.params.id)`; no ownership predicate; middleware `requireAuth` only checks the session exists (src/middleware/auth.js:10).
findings.impact: Any user can enumerate sequential IDs and read every customer's invoices (PII, amounts).
validation_steps: Start the app locally with seed data (npm run dev; two seeded users A and B).
Log in as user A and request GET /api/invoices/<id owned by B>.
Observe HTTP 200 with B's invoice. Expected: 404.
findings.remediation: Scope every query by tenant/owner: Invoice.findOne({ where: { id, accountId: req.user.accountId } }); add a policy layer with default deny.

triage.reason: Value is a public test fixture key in tests/; not loaded in production builds.
Traced request.args['url'] to requests.get with no allowlist (app.py:35). id-based triage must name the rule_id; prefer fingerprints.

attack_paths.title: SSRF to cloud credential theft
attack_paths.narrative: User-controlled URL fetch (SSRF) combined with IMDSv1 being allowed lets an attacker retrieve instance role credentials from 169.254.169.254.

checklist_results.notes: Requires concurrent requests against a running instance; no authorized environment

limitations: No running environment was available; runtime authorization behaviour is inferred from code.
Third-party payment provider integration reviewed from client code only.
